proof_review: Complete approved Theorem 26.1.5 compared in actual text and images, including its final arbitrary-order graph transfer. All nine books and ordinary citations remain valid.
All 23 original obligations, 15 original displays, three complete original solutions and original diagram retained.
The Fourier profile is smooth across the cutoff, polynomially bounded and defines an actual tempered distribution, including zero-dimensional Gaussian factors.
Exact Gaussian exponents give every negative Sobolev order and logarithmic failure of L2. Gaussian and polar constants use actual earlier proofs.
All mixed derivatives retain exact lambda exponents; compact cutoff integration by parts has the required vanishing remainder for every derivative.
Global L2 away from the origin covers both unbounded transverse and time directions and the k0 case, so the failure is local at the origin.
Off-cone Gaussian decay and actual W1 convolution locate the single positive wavefront direction. Weighted Young bounds and finite angular covering prove failure at the exact order.

Explicit rational time coordinate and locally finite normalized integer partition have positive denominators, compact time supports and shrinking transverse radii. Their sum is exactly one near the open axis.
The negative product norm uses the joint Fourier weight and actual compact multiplication, with the exact tensor-wavefront formula.
One sufficiently small mollifier scale meets all support, norm and finitely many differentiated conic seminorm constraints. Tail domination and bounded-frequency convergence are separate.
Summability in every negative Sobolev norm uses complete weighted L2 and yields one common tempered-distribution limit. Compact support includes both endpoint base points.
All off-direction Fourier seminorms are summable and agree with the Fourier transform of that actual distributional limit; endpoint covectors cannot introduce another direction.
Smooth convolution and the local finiteness of enlarged supports give the exact interior constant-factor model; actual order-zero failure reaches both endpoints by openness.
Pseudolocality gives endpoint forcing inclusion and complete model propagation across each endpoint forces both rays to occur.
Full proper graph pair of orders minus s and s retains every lower order, exact failure at s, and both solution wavefront inclusions.
Both ordered intertwining identities use actual CT19-CT20 defects and nested full graph supports, not equality of principal symbols. They give both directions of forcing equality.
Positive elliptic order reduction preserves the compact injective cosphere image and endpoints through a smooth positive finite reparametrization, for every real m.
All three unchanged solutions retain the full threshold criterion, both temporal jump directions, proper averaging, closed covector limit and graph-order sign.
Original figure coordinates represent the normalized base segment and endpoint forcing exactly. Cone boundaries are estimate bounds; scaled coordinate axes and exclusions are explicit.

Six finite groups check profile exponents, Gaussian normalization, differentiated amplitudes, explicit partition, both temporal Fourier signs and SVG geometry; these do not replace the mathematical review.
